liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Other One** (3 reviews): Entering the Mind Left Body jam, Jerry lands a beat behind the band, per the reviewer; Reviewer hears one of the grooviest Dead passages in The Other One, perhaps just before Mind Left Body [12][16][17]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (2 reviews): Reviewer praises the lovely transition from China Cat into I Know You Rider; Reviewer finds the China Cat into Rider transition sublime, with Jerry's guitar work at a peak [17][19]
- **To Lay Me Down** (1 review): Reviewer calls this the best available version, neither dragging nor wandering [14]
- **Greatest Story Ever Told** (1 review): Reviewer rates this among the best performances of the song they have heard [18]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd73-11-20 s1t01 Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd73-11-20 s1t02 Ramble On Rose**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd73-11-20 s1t03 Mexicali Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd73-11-20 s1t04 Don't Ease Me In**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd73-11-20 s1t05 Black Throated Wind**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd73-11-20 s1t06 Brown Eyed Women**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd73-11-20 s1t07 Beat It On Down The Line**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd73-11-20 s1t08 To Lay Me Down**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]

## The recordings

- **gd1973-11-20.144265.sbd.boswell.smith.miller.clugston.flac1648** (recommended): soundboard; 32 songs; 220 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd73-11-20.sbd.hollister.1234.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 31 songs; 200 min; rated 4.79/5 by 19 [4]. Said about its sound: Soundboard has clean, clear instruments, hiss-free, with Phil's bass strongly forward; Instrument mix is strong, with Keith's piano audible over the guitars, but the vocals sit low; Crisp soundboard with every instrument well placed in the mix, though vocals are somewhat low [13][15][17]
- **gd1973-11-20.sbd-patched.sirmick.76616.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 31 songs; 201 min; rated 5/5 by 7 [5]
- **gd73-11-20.wolfson.warner.22879.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 31 songs; 206 min; rated 4.5/5 by 8 [6]. Said about its sound: Audience recording is muddy and weak; other audience tapes, even older than 1973, sound better; Audience tape improves as the crowd quiets, ending up nearly soundboard-like [18][19]

## Around the show

- Reviewer pairs this show with the next night's as showing the band's stage of development in late 1973 [9]
- Reviewer says the show is overshadowed by the 11-11 and 11-17 shows from the same month [14]
- Late 1973 shows like this one show big gains over early 1973 in guitar tone, sound and playing [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1973-11-20.144265.sbd.boswell.smith.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Will Boswell; transferred by Matt Smith, Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Master Soundboard Cassettes > Will Boswell's 1st generation Reels @ 3.75 ips [1]. Also: Notes speculate that another cassette generation may exist before Will Boswell's reels [1]
- **gd73-11-20.sbd.hollister.1234.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [4]
- **gd1973-11-20.sbd-patched.sirmick.76616.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by SirMick; source: S:MR > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN (shnid 1234) [5]. Also: Patch for this song came from Cary Wolfson's audience tape, made with a Sony one-point stereo mic and TC-124; Fixes included adding 20 seconds of crowd and tuning at the start and repairing a brief left-channel dropout [5]
- **gd73-11-20.wolfson.warner.22879.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Cary Wolfson; transferred by A > D by David Minches; source: Audience Recording [6]
